A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EGAgent in Agentic Very Long Video Understanding. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original EGAgent evaluations on EgoLifeQA and Video-MME (Long), alongside tool ablations, retrieval analyses, oracle experiments and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds storage measurements and a manual audit of extracted graph relationships.

M1.justification: The graph schema, temporal annotation, planning and retrieval procedures remain unchanged. The new fusion prompts document a step already described in v1; the introduction's node-to-edge correction agrees with v1's existing formal method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same EgoLifeQA data and Video-MME (Long) subset. The new graph audit uses existing EgoLife relationships; newly disclosed duration and transcript-availability counts do not establish changed dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables and appendix analyses. SiLVR is newly cited in related work but is not added to any reported experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix D.5 adds a protocol randomly sampling 100 of 13,968 EgoLife relationships for manual verification against video and transcripts. D.4 introduces per-tool disk-storage measurements. Existing benchmark models, frame sampling and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds storage-cost analysis and a graph-quality audit with error characterization in Appendices D.4–D.5. Appendix E also newly describes exploratory relation-granularity experiments qualitatively. The existing tool ablations, oracle experiments and retrieval analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state in Appendix E that accuracies come from a single run. Neither adds confidence intervals, repeated-seed statistics or significance tests; the new audit reports only a point estimate.

E6.justification: Table 5 replaces GPT-4.1 EG+F+T HabitInsight/RelationMap/TaskMaster scores of 53.6/66.7/50.7% with 55.7/53.6/66.7%, matching Table 1, and D.1 revises the corresponding gains. v2 adds 94% audit accuracy, storage results and qualitative relation-granularity findings. Headline benchmark scores remain 57.5% and 74.1%.

T1.justification: The task formulation, graph definitions and Equations (1)–(5), and Appendix D.3's recall definition are unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about temporal entity graphs, agentic cross-modal reasoning, state-of-the-art EgoLifeQA performance and competitive Video-MME (Long) performance.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly argues that coarse relations reduce synonym fragmentation and improve robustness to noisy inputs, and that prompt-defined schemas support domain adaptation. D.5 identifies captioning and fusion errors more specifically than v1's general upstream-error limitation. These additions expand interpretation without quantified validation of the broader adaptability assertions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, supplies previously omitted caption–transcript fusion prompts, and corrects the transcript-search node identifier in the example code. It also discloses exact frame counts, transcript availability and storage footprints. These improve documentation of the retained pipeline.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SiLVR and briefly describes its caption-compression and language-based reasoning approach. Other reference changes, including RAVU's publication update, concern already-cited works rather than new research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar, terminology and cross-reference edits, clarifies the internship attribution, expands appendix explanations, and adds the Entity Graph Noise subsection. The main narrative and section ordering remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The figures and numbered table structures are retained. Changes include corrected best-score emphasis in Table 5, clarified table captions, a new boxed fusion prompt, and local reflow of text and code listings.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves Table 5's inconsistency with Table 1, improves reproducibility documentation through fusion prompts and code-access information, and adds concrete storage measurements and a small graph-quality audit. These provide limited improvements in consistency and empirical support. The main benchmark evidence is unchanged, while the 100-relationship audit and qualitative schema discussion leave broader robustness and adaptability only partly supported.
